To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the resonant x-ray scattering spectra of iron orthoborates in the vicinity of iron K edge are dominated by interference of x-rays diffracted from two inequivocal crystallographic sites.

resonant scattering of x-rays by two crystallographically distinct iron sites in Fe3BO6 gives rise to a number of ‘forbidden’ Bragg reflections, which can be used as a probe to investigate the local structure of the compound.

the resonant scattering of x-rays from two inequivalently occupied crystallographic sites gives rise to complex energy spectra of the ‘forbidden’ Bragg reflections, which depend strongly on the azimuthal angle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed study of the x-ray resonant scattering of a particular crystal structure.
the study of the resonant scattering properties of iron ions in Fe3BO6 in the vicinity of their absorption edge.
the study of a new phenomenon in resonant x‐ray diffraction, namely, the interference of x‐rays scattered from different atomic sites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the observed azimuthal dependences in the pre-edge energy region are a consequence of the inequivalent crystal positions of Fe ions, and that the azimuthal dependences are not a consequence of magnetic order.
the present work demonstrates the potential of resonant x-ray scattering for the study of the structure and magnetism of iron orthoborates.

resonant x-ray scattering from iron orthoborate is a very complex phenomenon, which can be understood only if all the relevant parameters of the system, i.e. crystal structure, magnetic order, absorption and thermal vibrations, are taken into consideration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, with a few exceptions, the resonant x-ray spectra of Fe3BO 6 are dominated by the interplay of inequivalence and anisotropy, both of which are related to the site specific character of resonant scattering.
the resonant x-ray scattering technique is a powerful tool for investigating the structure of complex materials.
the interplay of inequivalence of atomic positions and resonant x-ray scattering can be exploited to obtain detailed information about local structure and electronic properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of resonant x-ray scattering, it is not always possible to separate different effects and to assign them to a single scattering process.

the resonant scattering from two inequivalence sites in a crystal can be used to extract the site specific x-ray absorption spectrum, and the results can be further used to extract the local environment of each of the sites.
the azimuthal dependence of the resonant diffraction intensities can provide a wealth of information on the atomic and electronic structure of a given crystal.
